desc:
A Magento store audit with a fix list shows you what is slowing, exposing or limiting your shop, sorted by importance. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your Magento store from the front and the admin, then writes the findings in plain words with a clear fix for each.

## What is a Magento store audit?

A Magento store audit is a structured review of how your shop is built and run. It checks speed, the Magento version and patch status, installed extensions, search engine basics, catalog setup, the checkout and payment path, admin accounts and backups. The output is a written report that lists each problem, explains why it matters and says how to fix it.

Think of it as a service record for the store. You learn the true state of things before spending money on changes.

## Why Magento stores drift out of shape

Magento stores collect changes over time. Extensions are added for one-off needs, patches are skipped because nobody owns the task, and old admin users stay active after staff leave. Each decision made sense at the time, yet together they produce a slow site with hidden risks.

Without a review, owners often fix the loudest symptom and miss the cause. A slow category page might blame the host when the real issue is an extension that runs a heavy query on every load.

## How an audit improves results

An audit improves results by pointing effort at the right place. If the checkout fails for one payment method on mobile, fixing it matters more than a new banner. If product pages share the same title text, search engines struggle to tell them apart. If backups never ran, one failed update becomes a crisis.

Sorting findings by priority also saves money. You can start with a small number of high-impact fixes, then schedule the rest. We describe what each fix improves, and we do not promise rankings or revenue, since traffic, products and competitors all play a part.

## What a great Magento audit covers

- Page speed on desktop and mobile, with the reason behind each slow result.
- The installed Magento version and which security patches are applied.
- A list of extensions, including unused ones and signs of conflict between them.
- Titles, headings, canonical tags, sitemap and robots settings.
- Category and product setup, including attributes, images and duplicate content.
- A test of the cart, checkout and payment flow from a shopper's view.
- Admin users, roles and permissions, with accounts that should be removed.
- Backup routine and whether a restore has ever been tested.
- Theme and custom code, plus caching and server settings in the deeper package.
- A fix list ordered by priority, with each item written so a developer can act on it.

## How the audit works

You tell us the store address and what worries you most. We review the live storefront first, using real devices and speed tools, and then examine the admin with a limited user account. We never change settings during an audit.

We then write the report. Each finding has a short title, what we saw, why it matters and the recommended fix. Items are grouped into urgent, important and nice to have.

The Basic package is a quick health check of the storefront. The Standard package adds extensions, checkout, admin users and backups, with the full priority list. The Premium package goes further, with a code scan, server and caching review, a comparison with two competitor stores, a call and a step-by-step plan. You can add a call to a smaller package.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us about any problem your customers have mentioned.
- Share your analytics view so we can see which pages matter most.
- Decide who will carry out the fixes before the report arrives.
- Read the urgent items first and handle them quickly.
- Keep the report as a baseline for future reviews.

**Avoid:**
- Fixing issues while the audit is still being written.
- Judging the store only by how fast it loads on your own office network.
- Ignoring patch status because the shop looks fine.
- Adding new extensions to solve problems the report has not yet explained.
- Treating the lowest-priority items as a reason to delay the urgent ones.

## Who it is for

An audit suits an owner who inherited a Magento store and does not know what is inside it. It also suits a business planning a redesign or migration that wants to know what to fix first. A third case is a store that feels slower than it used to be and has no clear reason why.

## What we need from you

Send your store address and a read-only or limited admin user, added as a collaborator, staff or developer account where Magento and your host allow it. A short note on your top worries helps us focus. Please never share your password, and we make no changes to your store during the review.
